title: Meromorphic sections on a locally Noetherian scheme without embedded points
statement: Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme] [pqf-def-locnoeth] having no embedded points (every associated point of $\mathcal O_X$ is the generic point of an irreducible component of $X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]), and let $X^0$ be the set of generic points [def-sc-generic-point] of the irreducible components of $X$. Write $\mathcal K_X$ for the sheaf of meromorphic functions (the sheaf associated to localizing $\mathcal O_X$ at its non-zero-divisors) and, for an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal L$ [def-sc-invertible-module], $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)=\mathcal K_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal L$. Then for $\eta\in X^0$ the stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] are $\mathcal K_{X,\eta}=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ and $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)_\eta=\mathcal L_\eta$, and for every open $U\subseteq X$ the maps $$\mathcal K_X(U)\to\prod_{\eta\in X^0\cap U}\mathcal O_{X,\eta},\qquad \mathcal K_X(\mathcal L)(U)\to\prod_{\eta\in X^0\cap U}\mathcal L_\eta,$$ sending a section to its germs at the points of $X^0\cap U$, are bijective; they are compatible with restriction and with the module structure, $(ft)_\eta=f_\eta t_\eta$.

proof.text: The no-embedded-points hypothesis says every associated point of O_X is a generic point of an irreducible component. By [lem-sc-ass-weakass-locally-noetherian], this is also the assertion for weakly associated points. To check the finite-component hypothesis, let U be quasi-compact. Local Noetherianity gives a finite affine open cover of U by Noetherian affine schemes; intersecting each member with U and applying [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian] gives Noetherian opens, and a finite union of Noetherian opens is Noetherian. Therefore U has a Noetherian underlying space and hence finitely many irreducible components by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components]. Thus the hypotheses of [lem-sc-meromorphic-weakass-generic-product] hold, and it gives the product descriptions of K_X and K_X(L).

source.place: Tag 0EMH (divisors-lemma-quasi-coherent-K), statement and proof of part (1)

proof.text: At a generic point eta, the primes of O_{X,eta} are the generalizations of eta, so there is only the maximal prime; hence this local ring has dimension zero and is Artinian. Its maximal ideal is the nilradical, so every non-unit is nilpotent and therefore a zero-divisor. Consequently every non-zero-divisor is a unit, and the multiplicative set used to define K_X at eta consists only of units. The stalk of the sheafified localization is therefore K_{X,eta}=O_{X,eta}, since a stalk of the sheafification is the stalk of the presheaf and localization commutes with the filtered colimit defining the stalk (elementary; compare the proof of Tag 0EMF: in a local ring of dimension zero any nonzerodivisor is a unit). If eta lies in an open U, then j_eta^{-1}(U)=Spec O_{X,eta}, while if eta is not in U it is empty, since eta has no proper generalization. Evaluating the product on U therefore gives the first displayed product, with its map identified with the germ map.

source.place: Tag 0EMF (divisors-lemma-meromorphic-weakass-finite), proof: K_Y = O_Y for local rings of dimension zero

proof.text: For an invertible module L, the second product description in [lem-sc-meromorphic-weakass-generic-product] gives K_X(L)(U)=product_{eta in X^0 intersect U} L_eta. Taking stalks commutes with tensor products of O_X-modules, (K_X tensor L)_eta = K_{X,eta} tensor L_eta = O_{X,eta} tensor L_eta = L_eta (elementary, Modules Tag 01CE: both sides are filtered colimits of the section-wise tensor products), and with the module action rule in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] this sends a pure tensor f tensor t to f_eta tensor t_eta, which is the germ of ft; by additivity this gives (ft)_eta=f_eta t_eta. The same stalk rule shows these identifications commute with restriction maps.
